title: Spanish Wedding Phrases: Congratulations, Toasts and Vows
seo_title: Spanish Wedding Phrases: Congratulations, Toasts and Vows
meta_description: Spanish wedding phrases for guests and couples: congratulations, toasts, ¡vivan los novios!, card messages, vows, wedding vocabulary and cultural traditions.
excerpt: From ¡Vivan los novios! to card messages: everything to say at a Spanish-speaking wedding.

body_html:
Spanish wedding phrases come in handy whether you are a guest, a member of the wedding party or the one getting married. Weddings in Spanish-speaking countries are joyful, long and loud, often lasting well into the night, and there are traditional phrases for every moment: congratulating the couple, writing in the card, giving a toast and cheering ¡Vivan los novios!. Here’s what to say, and when.

Key takeaways
  • Congratulate the couple with ¡Felicidades! (everywhere) or ¡Enhorabuena! (Spain).
  • The classic cheer is ¡Vivan los novios!
  • Card messages wish happiness: Que sean muy felices.
  • The bride and groom are los novios.
{{toc}}

Wedding vocabulary

SpanishEnglish
la boda (el casamiento in some countries)wedding
los noviosthe bride and groom (also: boyfriend and girlfriend)
la novia / el noviobride / groom
los padrinosthe sponsors (often the groom’s mother and bride’s father in Spain)
la dama de honorbridesmaid
el banquetereception, wedding meal
la luna de mielhoneymoon
casarse conto marry

The RAE dictionary notes that novio means both a boyfriend and a groom, which is why los novios on the wedding day means the couple. Note the preposition: Se casa con Laura, not a Laura. See {{link:spanish-preposition-mistakes|Spanish preposition mistakes}}.

Congratulating the couple

  • ¡Felicidades a los dos! Congratulations to you both!
  • ¡Que sean muy felices! I hope you’ll be very happy!
  • ¡Enhorabuena! and ¡Que seáis muy felices! Congratulations, be very happy! (Spain, with vosotros)
  • ¡Qué guapa estás! You look beautiful! (to the bride)
  • Ha sido una ceremonia preciosa. It was a beautiful ceremony.

More general congratulations in {{link:congratulations-in-spanish|congratulations in Spanish}}.

{{image:2}}

Spanish wedding phrases for the card

  • Les deseamos toda la felicidad del mundo. We wish you all the happiness in the world.
  • Que su amor crezca cada día. May your love grow every day.
  • Gracias por dejarnos compartir este día tan especial. Thank you for letting us share this special day.
  • Por una vida llena de amor, risas y aventuras. To a life full of love, laughter and adventures.
  • Con mucho cariño, With much love,

In Spain, friends use the vosotros forms instead: Os deseamos…, Que vuestro amor crezca…. See {{link:tu-vs-usted|tú vs usted}} for vosotros and ustedes.

Toasts and cheers

  • ¡Vivan los novios! Long live the bride and groom! (everyone answers ¡Vivan!)
  • ¡Que se besen! Kiss! Kiss! (guests chant this)
  • Quiero brindar por… I’d like to make a toast to…
  • ¡Por los novios! To the bride and groom!
  • ¡Salud! Cheers!

A short toast

Buenas noches a todos. Conozco a Carlos desde hace quince años y nunca lo había visto tan feliz como desde que conoció a Marta. Marta, gracias por hacerlo tan feliz. Les deseo una vida llena de amor. ¡Por los novios!

{{book:love-slowly}}

Vows and ceremony phrases

  • Sí, quiero. I do.
  • Yo, Ana, te tomo a ti, Luis, como esposo… I, Ana, take you, Luis, to be my husband…
  • …en la salud y en la enfermedad, en lo bueno y en lo malo… in sickness and in health, for better or for worse…
  • Los declaro marido y mujer. I now pronounce you husband and wife.
  • Puedes besar a la novia. You may kiss the bride.

Traditions you might see

  • Las arras: thirteen coins exchanged during the ceremony, a symbol of shared prosperity (Spain, Mexico and elsewhere).
  • El lazo: a rope or rosary placed around the couple’s shoulders (Mexico, Philippines).
  • El ramo: the bride’s bouquet, sometimes given to a special person rather than thrown.
  • Late nights: dinner may start at 10 p.m. and dancing continue until dawn, followed by churros con chocolate or la recena.
  • Gifts: in Spain, guests often give money by bank transfer or in an envelope rather than gifts from a list.

A sample conversation

  • Guest: ¡Felicidades, chicos! ¡Estuvo preciosa la boda! (Congratulations, guys! It’s been a beautiful wedding!)
  • Bride: ¡Gracias! Nos da mucho gusto que estén aquí. (Thank you! We’re so happy you’re here.)
  • Guest: ¡Que sean muy felices! Y ahora… ¡a bailar! (May you be very happy! And now… let’s dance!)

Invitations and RSVPs

Wedding invitations in Spanish often begin with the parents’ names: Los padres de los novios tienen el placer de invitarle a la boda de sus hijos… (The parents of the bride and groom have the pleasure of inviting you to the wedding of their children…). To reply: Confirmo mi asistencia (I confirm I’ll attend), Allí estaremos (We’ll be there) or, if you can’t go, Lamentablemente no podremos asistir, pero les deseamos un día maravilloso (Unfortunately we won’t be able to attend, but we wish you a wonderful day).

What to wear and what to give

Spanish-speaking weddings are often more formal than you might expect: suits and ties for men, and elegant dresses for women, with white reserved for the bride. In Spain, guests commonly give money, either in an envelope (un sobre) or by bank transfer to the account printed on the invitation. In Mexico and other countries, a gift list (la mesa de regalos) is common. If you’re unsure, ask a friend: ¿Qué se suele regalar en las bodas aquí? (What do people usually give at weddings here?)

Final thoughts

Congratulate warmly, write a heartfelt card, raise your glass and shout ¡Vivan los novios! with everyone else. Then dance until the churros arrive. For more life moments, see {{link:spanish-phrases-for-everyday-situations|my guide to Spanish phrases for everyday situations}}.

faq.q: How do you congratulate a couple on their wedding in Spanish?
faq.a: ¡Felicidades!, followed by ¡Que sean muy felices! In Spain: ¡Enhorabuena! and ¡Que seáis muy felices!
Long live the bride and groom! It’s the traditional cheer at Spanish-speaking weddings; guests reply ¡Vivan!

faq.q: What do you write in a wedding card in Spanish?
faq.a: Les deseamos toda la felicidad del mundo (Os deseamos… in Spain), plus a personal line.
